display.purpose: The hero headline of the landing, the docs home and Meeting At 10, once per page; 44px rising to 72px.

body-large.purpose: Leads and section descriptions, held to about 34 to 40rem.

body.purpose: Reading text and the comfortable-density default; long-form text stops at 680px.

body-small.purpose: Card bodies, block text, alert bodies and the compact-density default.

label.purpose: Field labels, tabs, navbar links, and alert and toast titles.

caption.purpose: Badges, meta rows and notes; navigation group labels use it at 600.

time.purpose: Time codes (09:00-10:30), room codes (CCS 304) and references (DEMO-024); tabular, slashed zero.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: Hovered or dragged blocks and slots, hovered linked cards, hovered primary and destructive buttons, the chosen segment, the switch thumb and tooltips (light theme).

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: Menus, listboxes, popovers, dialogs, drawers, toasts and overlay cards (light theme).

shadows.name: lift-dark
shadows.purpose: The lift in the dark theme.

shadows.name: overlay-dark
shadows.purpose: The overlay in the dark theme, on the raised slate (#22304A), with a 1px top highlight.

shadows.name: top-highlight
shadows.purpose: Top edge of solid buttons, current navigation items, the chosen day and the current page number (light; 35% in dark).

shadows.name: top-highlight-dark
shadows.purpose: The top highlight in the dark theme.

shadows.name: plate-dark
shadows.purpose: Door plate edge in the dark theme (none in light).

motion.name: duration-quick
motion.purpose: Color, hover, border and focus changes; tooltips; small overlay exits.

motion.name: duration-base
motion.purpose: Scrim and panel fades, popover entrance, tab panel fade, neighbor dimming.

motion.name: duration-slow
motion.purpose: Dialog and toast rise; the chosen slot's fill swipe.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Entrances and hover: the exponential ease-out.

motion.name: ease-in-out
motion.purpose: Pending loops: the button sweep line, the skeleton pulse.

motion.name: ease-exit
motion.purpose: Things leaving: dialog, drawer, toast, popover.

motion.name: spring-snappy
motion.purpose: Stiffness 600, damping 49, mass 1; settles in 379ms (--ds-motion-spring-snappy-duration). Checks, switch thumb, radio dot, caret turns, block lift and drop, link arrows.

motion.name: spring-smooth
motion.purpose: Stiffness 420, damping 40, mass 1; settles in 416ms. Indicators sliding along rules (tabs, segments, day strip), progress and meter fills, disclosure height, layout glides.

motion.name: spring-gentle
motion.purpose: Stiffness 260, damping 32, mass 1; settles in 560ms. Drawers, bottom sheets, the dialog sheet on phones.

motion.name: distance-lift
motion.purpose: Hover lift of blocks, slots, linked cards and solid buttons.

motion.name: distance-drop
motion.purpose: Blocks dropping into their cells, once, staggered 25ms.

motion.name: now-line-glide
motion.purpose: The now-line and its gutter time move each time the clock updates (every 30 seconds); the glide is dropped under reduced motion.

motion.name: isolate-dim
motion.purpose: Neighbors of a hovered, focused or chosen block dim one step.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion: no travel, no loops; states land at once.

breakpoints.name: tablet
breakpoints.purpose: 8 columns, 24px gutters and margins; dialogs stop being bottom sheets; steppers go horizontal.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.purpose: Component switch: navbar links leave the menu sheet, agenda rows gain a third column, split section headers.

breakpoints.name: desktop
breakpoints.purpose: 12 columns, 24px gutters, 32px margins; app shell shows sidebar and top bar; hero splits 5:7.

materials.name: hatch
materials.value: repeating-linear-gradient(135deg, color-mix(in srgb, var(--ds-hatch-ink) 45%, transparent) 0 1px, transparent 1px 7px)
materials.purpose: Taken and restricted fills; 55% in dark. Words on it ride on paper labels.

materials.name: hatch-strong
materials.value: repeating-linear-gradient(135deg, color-mix(in srgb, var(--ds-hatch-ink) 80%, transparent) 0 1px, transparent 1px 7px)
materials.purpose: Small hatched markers: restricted lane chips, legend swatches, timeline markers; 90% in dark.

materials.name: rule-minor
materials.purpose: Half-hour rules on the week sheet.

materials.name: today-bg
materials.purpose: Today's column tint on the week sheet.

materials.name: scrim
materials.purpose: The veil behind dialogs and drawers.

narrative.overview:
The system is the weekly consultation timetable taped to a faculty door in the College of Computer Studies, rebuilt as an interface. Every surface it serves (the ACCS landing, the ACCS portal and admin, the Meeting At 10 site and the showcase docs) is a paper-white sheet on a cool canvas, ruled with hairlines that form real time grids, and its content arrives as blocks placed in time. A block's lane color owns its whole fill: navy for the schedule and for action, violet for community, teal for consultations. The fourth lane, restricted reports, has no hue. It is hatched ink with words, drawn into the grid where everyone can see where the boundary runs.

The voice is structured and calm, and it reads at a glance. Plus Jakarta Sans at 800 with tight tracking gives headings the weight of a painted name plate, Inter carries reading and interface text, and JetBrains Mono appears only where a clock or a filing system would print. State is drawn as line form: a solid edge is open, a dashed edge is pending, hatching is taken or restricted, a strike is closed, and a word always comes with the line. The page you are on becomes a solid navy block. The present moment is a red line with the time on a small plate.

Sheets rest flat on a 1px rule. Only blocks being handled and overlays floating above the page cast shadows, ink-tinted in light and black with a 1px top highlight in dark. Motion is quick and physical: 120ms color changes, critically damped springs for anything that slides along a rule, overlays that rise 8px on an exponential ease-out, and under reduced motion every state lands at once. The system must never feel playful or gamified, like a generic SaaS template, cold or bureaucratic, or slowed down by motion.
keyCharacteristics: Paper-white sheets (12px corners, 1px hairline) on a cool canvas, flat at rest.
Blocks placed in time: solid lane fills, 6px corners, a tabular mono time code on top.
Three hued lanes and one unhued lane: navy schedule, violet community, teal consultations, hatched restricted reports.
State drawn in line form (solid, dashed, hatched, struck), always with a word.
The Meeting At 10 calendar as the system's logo: a navy calendar whose paper page holds a blue appointment block with a white 10; in dark, a light frame around a navy page.
The door plate as the ACCS wordmark: a navy name plate lettered in white Plus Jakarta Sans 800.
A red now-line marks the present on every time grid.
Light and dark themes with an OS fallback, comfortable and compact density, and every state kept visible under forced colors and reduced motion.

rules.name: The Lane Owns the Block Rule
rules.body: Schedule is navy, community violet, consultations teal. The lane color fills the whole block, chip or tile at full strength; it is never thinned to a stripe, a dot or a tinted edge.

rules.name: The No-Hue Boundary Rule
rules.body: The restricted reports lane has no hue: neutral ink, hatching and a word. Color never signals confidentiality, privacy or permission, and a lane color never implies access.

rules.name: The Mono Is a Clock Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono appears only where a clock or a filing system would print: times, room codes, references, keys and code, always with tabular, slashed-zero numerals. Everything else is Inter or Plus Jakarta Sans.

rules.name: The Heading Carries Itself Rule
rules.body: Page and section headings stand alone, with no kicker or eyebrow above them: size, Plus Jakarta Sans weight (800 or 700) and space carry the hierarchy, and context goes in the description below. Two things that sit above titles are not kickers: the brand mark (the Meeting At 10 logo, or the door plate on ACCS surfaces), and the head line of a block or card (time code, lane chip), which is item metadata.

rules.name: The Real Grid Rule
rules.body: Where a grid is drawn, it is a real, labeled time grid: hours down the side, days across the top. Hairlines are never decoration, and the hour row (48px, 40px compact) shares the 8px module with the controls.

rules.name: The Declared Once Rule
rules.body: At rest, every surface declares its elevation once: a 1px rule or a shadow, never both. Sheets and cards rest flat on their rule, overlays float on a shadow with no rule, and a linked card trades its rule for the lift on hover. A line-form edge is a state mark, not a rule, and stays when its block lifts.

rules.name: The Earned Lift Rule
rules.body: Content never rests lifted: blocks, slots, buttons and linked cards cast the lift shadow only while hovered, dragged or chosen. The only parts resting on it are small pieces riding a track (the switch thumb, the chosen segment) and the tooltip plate. Elevation shows interaction and layering, never importance, security or privacy.

rules.name: The Material Radius Rule
rules.body: Radius follows the material, not the component: chip 4px, block and plate 6px, control 8px, sheet 12px, overlay 16px. Full rounding is kept for dots and toggles: the now-dot, today and unread dots, avatars, radios, switches, step markers and progress tracks.

rules.name: The Line Form Rule
rules.body: Status and availability are drawn as lines: solid for open, active or done; dashed for pending, draft or upcoming; hatched for taken or restricted; struck for disabled, closed, unavailable or withdrawn. A word always comes with the line.

rules.name: The Current Is Solid Rule
rules.body: The page you are on, the chosen day and the current page number become the solid navy block, with the icon in its fill weight; a chosen time block or slot fills solid in its own lane color. Hovering a navigation item, option or row takes a highlighter wash instead.

rules.name: The Now Is a Line Rule
rules.body: The present moment on a time grid is a 2px Now-Line Red line with an 8px dot and the time on a small red plate. It glides as the clock updates and drops the glide under reduced motion.

dos: Do write every color as a semantic or treatment token (`var(--ds-action-default)`, `var(--ds-hatch)`); the frontmatter keys are those token names, and the token check rejects raw hex in product code.
Do put scheduled things on a ruled sheet as blocks in lanes: the lane color as the whole fill, the time code on top in tabular JetBrains Mono, the title in Inter 600, meta last.
Do pair every line form with a word ("Open", "Awaiting confirmation", "Booked", "Unavailable") and every status tone with a label.
Do hatch taken and restricted areas (1px diagonal hairlines every 7px) and set their words on small paper labels so the lines never cross text.
Do keep one solid navy primary button per task region, and use the ruled secondary and the tertiary wash for everything else.
Do make the current page, the chosen day and the current page number the solid navy block with a fill-weight icon, and let a chosen block or slot fill with its own lane color.
Do keep the 2px focus ring with its 2px gap (Focus Blue #3157D5, #97B5FF in dark) visible on every interactive element.
Do keep controls on the 8px module (40, 48 or 56px), at least 44px on coarse pointers, with 16px text in inputs.
Do let color and hover changes take 120ms, slide indicators on the smooth spring, raise overlays 8px on the exponential ease-out, and land every state instantly under reduced motion.

Do use the Meeting At 10 calendar logo as the system's own mark (the theme-aware `Logo`, or the light, dark and auto files as exported), and the door plate (navy plate, white Plus Jakarta Sans 800) as the ACCS wordmark until an ACCS logo is approved.
donts: Don't add a colored stripe along the side of a card, alert or row; alerts are tinted sheets with a solid icon block. The 2px lines the world draws (the now-line, selected-tab and current-link rules, stepper and case-timeline rails) mark time and position, not decoration.
Don't put a kicker or eyebrow label above a page or section heading; context goes in the description beneath it. The door plate is the ACCS wordmark, not a kicker.
Don't give a resting surface both a rule and a shadow.
Don't let hue alone carry status, severity, availability or permission, and never give the restricted lane a hue.
Don't set labels, headings, navigation or buttons in JetBrains Mono.
Don't nest cards, or build page structure from rows of same-size icon cards; use Agenda rows, sections, rules and headings.
Don't use gradient text, glass, glow or colored shadows; the hatch and the ruled grid are the only drawn patterns.
Don't use emoji or Unicode glyphs as icons; use the Phosphor set and its weights.
Don't hold content back until it animates in; entrances start from a visible state, and only overlays fade.
Don't recolor the door plate with a lane color, style it as a seal or crest, or redraw the proposed ACCS logo files.
Don't put the light Meeting At 10 artwork on a dark ground, recolor the mark beyond its light, dark and auto versions, or use its identity colors in the interface.
Don't use more than one door-plate band on a page.
